<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><b>AMES NATIONAL CORPORATION </b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt;"><b>ANNOUNCES EARNINGS FOR THE <font style="text-transform:uppercase;"><a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602745552">first</a> </font>QUARTER OF <a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603461404">2026</a> </b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Ames, Iowa &#8211; Ames National Corporation (Nasdaq: ATLO; the &#8220;Company&#8221;) today reported net income for the&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> of <a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720531669118" originalfact="$6.0" scale-include-commas="false" scale-precision="1" scale-round="false" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$6.0</a>&nbsp;million, or <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720531697909">$0.67</a>&nbsp;per share, compared to <a data-tblloc="2x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720531713794" originalfact="$3.4" scale-include-commas="false" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$3.4</a>&nbsp;million, or <a data-tblloc="3x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720531753302">$0.39</a>&nbsp;per share, earned in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a>.&nbsp;The <a data-tblloc="2x5" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2025331743701343047">increase</a>&nbsp;in earnings is primarily&nbsp;due to an increase in net interest income and decrease in credit loss expense.&nbsp;Net interest income increased due to higher yields and average balances&nbsp;on&nbsp;investments, combined with a lower cost of funds driven by declining market rates and reduced borrowings. The decrease in credit loss expense was primarily due to a decline in loan balances in the first quarter of 2026 and a specific reserve placed on a commercial loan relationship in 2025.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><a data-tblloc="44x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602891997">First</a> quarter <a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> loan interest income was&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="4x3" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720544564312" originalfact="$142" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$142</a>&nbsp;thousand higher than <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a> and was primarily due to improved yield on the loan portfolio. Interest income from investment securities increased by $1.1&nbsp;million&nbsp;during this same period due to higher average balances and maturities reinvested at higher rates. Deposit interest expense decreased&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="5x3" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2025991760040941546">$1.1</a> million during this same period due primarily to decreases in market rates. Other borrowed funds interest expense decreased&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="11x3" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720545164791">$334</a>&nbsp;thousand during the same period due primarily to reduced borrowings.&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="44x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602903100">First</a> quarter <a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> net interest income totaled&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720534749024" originalfact="$15.4" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$15.4</a> million, an&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="6x5" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720534889713">increase</a>&nbsp;of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="6x3" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720534896576" originalfact="$2.5" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$2.5</a> million, or <a data-tblloc="6x4" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2025331743708048829">19.5%</a>,&nbsp;compared to the same quarter a year ago. These factors were the primary contributors to the Company&#8217;s net interest margin, on a tax-equivalent basis (a non-GAAP measure),&nbsp;improving to&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="9x2" data-tblname="569098" data-tblv="11" id="led569098F2024691720534965072">3.01%</a> for the quarter ended&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604306375">March 31, 2026</a> as compared to&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="9x4" data-tblname="569098" data-tblv="11" id="led569098F2024691720534980401">2.53%</a> for the quarter ended <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604351594">March 31, 2025</a>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x2" data-tblname="569099" data-tblv="11" id="led569099F2024691720535125847">3.00%</a> for the quarter ended <a data-tblloc="64x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024691720535151503">December 31, 2025</a>. &nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">A credit loss benefit&nbsp;of (<a data-tblloc="7x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720535370532" originalfact="$347" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="false" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$347</a>)thousand was recognized in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> as compared to a credit loss expense of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="7x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720535413191" originalfact="$962" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="false" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$962</a> thousand in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a>. Net loan recoveries&nbsp;for the quarter ended&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a>&nbsp;totaled <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="569099" data-tblv="11" id="led569099F2024991728489993421">$32</a>&nbsp;thousand compared to net loan charge-offs totaled <a data-tblloc="3x2" data-tblname="569099" data-tblv="11" id="led569099F2025991760036447226">$48</a>&nbsp;thousand&nbsp;for the quarter ended <a data-tblloc="9x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F20246121720791254633">March 31, 2025</a>. The credit loss benefit&nbsp;in 2026&nbsp;was primarily due to a decline in loan balances. The credit loss expense in 2025 was primarily due to an increase in specific reserves in the commercial loan portfolio.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Noninterest income for the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> totaled&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="8x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720545816463" originalfact="$2.8" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$2.8</a> million as compared to&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="8x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720545843152" originalfact="$2.5" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$2.5</a> million in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a>, an <a data-tblloc="8x5" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720545871031">increase</a>&nbsp;of <a data-tblloc="8x4" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720545882387">9.3%</a>. The increase is primarily due to an increase in wealth management income due to growth in assets under management and an increase in estate and trust fees.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Noninterest expense for the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> totaled <a data-tblloc="9x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720556452979" originalfact="$10.9" scale-include-commas="false" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$10.9</a>&nbsp;million compared to <a data-tblloc="9x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720556466706" originalfact="$10.3" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$10.3</a>&nbsp;million recorded in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a>, an&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="9x5" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720556496586">increase</a> of <a data-tblloc="9x4" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720556484729">5.9%</a>. The increase reflects higher professional fees, salaries and benefits.&nbsp; The increase in professional fees was primarily due to $300&nbsp;thousand of&nbsp;consultant&nbsp;fees for certain contract negotiations in the first quarter of 2026. The&nbsp;consultant fees are expected to continue throughout 2026 as the negotiation is in process.&nbsp; The increase in salaries and benefits was&nbsp;driven by anticipated bonus payouts as Company performance thresholds are met.&nbsp;The efficiency ratio was <a data-tblloc="8x2" data-tblname="569098" data-tblv="11" id="led569098F2024691720556561069">59.69%</a>&nbsp;for the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> as compared to <a data-tblloc="8x4" data-tblname="569098" data-tblv="11" id="led569098F2024691720556570510">66.38%</a>&nbsp;in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a>. The efficiency ratio continues to improve as&nbsp;net interest margin increases.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Income tax expense for the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603320939">2026</a> totaled <a data-tblloc="10x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720556590483">$1.7</a>&nbsp;million compared to <a data-tblloc="10x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720556612683">$794</a>&nbsp;thousand recorded in the <a data-tblloc="45x1" data-tblname="562994" data-tblv="11" id="led562994F2024551717602764750">first</a> quarter of <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717603487161">2025</a>. The effective tax rate was <a data-tblloc="12x1" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024691720557078915">22%</a>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="12x2" data-tblname="563000" data-tblv="11" id="led563000F2024941728072137597">19%</a>&nbsp;for the quarters ended <a data-tblloc="7x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604336148">March 31, 2026 and 2025</a>, respectively. The increase in income tax expense and effective tax rate was primarily due to higher net income and lower New Markets Tax Credits. The final year of tax credits was 2025 for a majority of the New Markets Tax Credit&nbsp;projects.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"><b>Balance Sheet Review:</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a>, total assets were <a data-tblloc="2x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549388486" originalfact="$2.1" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$2.1</a>&nbsp;billion, a&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549424135">decrease</a>&nbsp;of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x3" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549434879" originalfact="$41.8" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="false" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$41.8</a>&nbsp;million, as compared to <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>. The&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="2x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549476304">decrease</a>&nbsp;in assets was primarily due to a&nbsp;decrease in interest-bearing deposits in financial institutions and loans receivable, partially offset by an increase in securities available-for-sale.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Securities available-for-sale as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a>&nbsp;increased to <a data-tblloc="3x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549501561" originalfact="$688.8" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$688.8</a>&nbsp;million from <a data-tblloc="3x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549519355" originalfact="$640.4" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$640.4</a>&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>. The&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="3x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720549547027">increase</a> in securities available-for-sale is primarily due to purchases in excess of maturities and&nbsp;lower unrealized losses in the investment portfolio. The Company's investment portfolio had an expected duration of 3.2&nbsp;years as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a>. There are approximately $102&nbsp;million of investments maturing within one year at an average yield of approximately 1.5%.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Net loans as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a> decreased to <a data-tblloc="4x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550333080" originalfact="$1.26" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="2" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$1.26</a>&nbsp;billion as compared to <a data-tblloc="4x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550352279" originalfact="$1.31" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="2" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$1.31</a>&nbsp;billion as of <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>, a&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="4x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550381122">decrease</a>&nbsp;of <a data-tblloc="4x4" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550386611">3.2%</a>. The decrease was primarily due to payoffs in the commercial real estate portfolio and partially offset by an increase in the 1 to 4 family residential real estate portfolio.&nbsp;Substandard loans were $34.8&nbsp;million and $32.4&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="7x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2025331743709953886">March 31, 2026 and 2025</a>, respectively. Substandard-impaired loans were $19.6&nbsp;million and $15.7&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="7x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2025331743709962772">March 31, 2026 and 2025</a>, respectively. The increase in substandard loans is primarily due to weakening in the multi-family portfolio and partially offset by an improvement in the commercial real estate portfolio.&nbsp; Some multi-family real estate loans are experiencing a decline in occupancy rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in&nbsp;substandard-impaired loans is primarily due to two&nbsp;agricultural loan relationships.&nbsp;Loans past due 30 days or more totaled $19.4 million as of March 31, 2026, compared to $11.8&nbsp;million as of March 31, 2025.&nbsp;The increase is primarily related to two&nbsp;agricultural&nbsp;operating loan relationships classified as substandard-impaired and one construction&nbsp;real estate loan relationship that matured and is being restructured. There are approximately $350&nbsp;million of loans maturing within one year at an average yield of approximately 5.4%.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The allowance for credit losses on <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a> totaled <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550454643" originalfact="$17.4" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$17.4</a>&nbsp;million or <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2025331743710542952">1.36%</a>&nbsp;of loans, compared to <a data-tblloc="5x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2025331743710553295">$18.0</a>&nbsp;million, or&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="6x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2025331743710563764">1.36%</a> of loans, as of <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>. The&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="5x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550518957">decrease</a> in the allowance for credit losses is primarily due to a decrease in loan balances.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">Deposits totaled <a data-tblloc="7x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550547541" originalfact="$1.87" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="2" scale-round="false" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$1.87</a>&nbsp;billion as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a>, a&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="7x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550571936">decrease</a>&nbsp;of <a data-tblloc="7x4" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550578142">2.0%</a>, compared to <a data-tblloc="7x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550584703" originalfact="$1.91" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="2" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$1.91</a>&nbsp;billion recorded as of <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>. The <a data-tblloc="7x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550603878">decrease</a>&nbsp;in deposits is primarily due to a&nbsp;decrease in public funds and&nbsp;partially offset by higher&nbsp;balances in retail and commercial checking accounts. Securities sold under agreements to repurchase decreased to&nbsp;$36.7&nbsp;million as of March&nbsp;31, 2026, compared to&nbsp;$45.8&nbsp;million as of March&nbsp;31, 2025.&nbsp;Securities sold under agreements to repurchase and deposit balances fluctuate as customers&#8217; liquidity needs vary and could be impacted by prevailing market interest rates, competition, and economic conditions.&nbsp; Approximately 15% of deposits&nbsp;are tied to&nbsp;external indexes as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F20252261743014527245">March 31, 2026</a>. Deposit interest expense related to these deposits can be more volatile&nbsp;than other deposit products in a changing interest rate environment.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Other borrowings decreased to <a data-tblloc="8x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550643076" originalfact="$18.2" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$18.2</a>&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a> compared to <a data-tblloc="8x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550660159" originalfact="$35.8" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$35.8</a>&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>. The Company has continued to reduce&nbsp;borrowings&nbsp;as investments have matured and cash is redeployed.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s stockholders&#8217; equity represented <a data-tblloc="9x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2025691752095002457">9.7%</a>&nbsp;of total assets as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a> with all of the Company&#8217;s six affiliate banks considered well-capitalized as defined by federal capital regulations. Total stockholders&#8217; equity was <a data-tblloc="10x1" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550746782" originalfact="$207.6" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$207.6</a>&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604318227">March 31, 2026</a>, compared to <a data-tblloc="10x2" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550762607" originalfact="$183.1" scale-include-commas="true" scale-precision="1" scale-round="true" scale-show-unit="false" scale-unit="1">$183.1</a>&nbsp;million as of <a data-tblloc="6x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2024551717604366531">March 31, 2025</a>. The&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="10x5" data-tblname="562998" data-tblv="11" id="led562998F2024691720550785675">increase</a> in stockholders&#8217; equity of $24.5&nbsp;million was primarily the result of a decrease in unrealized losses on the investment portfolio and retention of net income in excess of dividends.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Share Repurchase Program</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">For the period January&nbsp;1, 2026&nbsp;through March&nbsp;31, 2026, under the repurchase program that was announced in August&nbsp;2025, which allowed for the repurchase of 200,000 shares of common stock, the Company did not repurchase any shares. There were 165,053 shares available to be repurchased under that repurchase program as of&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="5x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2025991760037682573">March 31, 2026</a>.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The weighted average outstanding shares for the three months ended&nbsp;<a data-tblloc="7x1" data-tblname="562995" data-tblv="11" id="led562995F2025991760037700872">March 31, 2026 and 2025</a> was 8,857,220&nbsp;and 8,917,386, respectively. The Company had no potentially dilutive securities outstanding during the periods presented.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Cash Dividend Announcement</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On February&nbsp;11, 2026, the Company declared a quarterly cash dividend on common stock, payable on March&nbsp;13, 2026&nbsp;to stockholders of record as of February&nbsp;27, 2026, equal to $0.24&nbsp;per share. The dividend is an increase of $0.04 per share or 20% from the prior quarter.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>AVERAGE BALANCES AND INTEREST RATES&nbsp;</b><i>(unaudited)</i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The following two tables are used to calculate the Company&#8217;s non-GAAP net interest margin on a fully taxable equivalent (FTE) basis. The first table includes the Company&#8217;s average assets and the related income to determine the average yield on earning assets. The second table includes the average liabilities and related expense to determine the average rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities. The net interest margin is equal to interest income less interest expense divided by average earning assets.</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Non-GAAP Financial Measures</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">This report contains references to financial measures that are not defined in GAAP.&nbsp;Such non-GAAP financial measures include the Company&#8217;s presentation of net interest income and net interest margin on an FTE&nbsp;basis. Management believes these non-GAAP financial measures are widely used in the financial institutions industry and provide useful information to both management and investors to analyze and evaluate the Company&#8217;s financial performance. Limitations associated with non-GAAP financial measures include the risks that persons might disagree as to the appropriateness of items included in these measures and that different companies might calculate these measures differently. These non-GAAP disclosures should not be considered an alternative to the Company&#8217;s GAAP results. The following table reconciles the non-GAAP financial measures of net interest income and net interest margin on an FTE basis to GAAP <i>(dollars in thousands)</i>.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
